name: AD — Shadow Credentials (msDS-KeyCredentialLink Modified)
description:
Attacker objective
Write a Key Credential (msDS-KeyCredentialLink) to an account to authenticate as it via PKINIT (Shadow Credentials / Whisker) — stealthy takeover and persistence.

Attack logic
This attribute is written only during legitimate key-based credential provisioning (for example Windows Hello for Business). A modification outside that process enables certificate-based impersonation of the target account.

Why this detection works
Directory-service change auditing (5136/5137) records modifications to msDS-KeyCredentialLink with the acting subject and the target object.

False positives
Legitimate Windows Hello for Business enrollment.

Tuning
Allowlist the WHfB provisioning service/account.

Required telemetry
Windows Security 5136/5137 (AttributeLDAPDisplayName=msDS-KeyCredentialLink, SubjectUserName, ObjectDN).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. SubjectUserName wrote the key credential; ObjectDN = the victim account.
2. Remove the KeyCredential, reset the target account, and investigate the subject and any PKINIT logons that followed.
false_positives: Legitimate Windows Hello for Business enrollment.
